This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR No.77/2016, under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Sadar Bazar, Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Learned ASC appears on advance notice, and accepts notice.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 21.11.2013 according to Muslim rites and ceremonies and they lived together as husband and wife with each other.
One male child was born out of the said wedlock on 03.08.2014.

sentences.text: Counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, petitioner no.1 has divorced respondent no.2 through three notices dated 24.12.2018, 28.01.2019 and 04.03.2019.
On 16.04.2019 divorce letter was issued by Qazi as per Shariyat Law.

sentences.text: Copy of the said settlement is placed on record.
Accordingly, on 06.01.2023, petitioner no.1 withdrew his case no. 4598/2020.

On 10.01.2023 maintenance petition under Section 123 Cr.P.C bearing no. 43/2017 was dismissed in lieu of the compromise arrived between the parties and at that time an amount of Rs.2,00,000/-
was given to respondent no.2 by way of demand draft by the petitioner.
He further submitted that on 17.01.2023, civil suit no. 856/2020 for permanent and mandatory injunction was withdrawn.

He further submitted that on 07.03.2023 complainant case bearing no. 3222/2017 was dismissed as compromised in pursuance of the settlement and Rs.3,00,000/- was given to the respondent no.2 by way of demand draft by the petitioner.
Hence the present petition for quashing of aforesaid FIR.

5. Petitioners and respondent no.2 are present in Court today and they have been identified by the IO as the petitioners reside in the jurisdiction of P.S.Sadar Bazar, in which SI Parveen Kumar is posted.
IO states that he has visited the house of the petitioners 15 days ago in order to verify the factum of filing of this petition.
On my query from SI whether he has made This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/09/2023 at 11:00:38 departure and arrival entries when he visited the house of petitioners, to which he states that he has not made any entries.
IO is directed to remain careful in future in this regard.
6. I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent No.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioners.
She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion.
As per settlement, today, a demand draft of Rs. 4,00,000/- (bearing no. 369566 dated 01.05.2023 drawn on Yes Bank Ltd.) has been handed over to respondent no.2.
Respondent No.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
7. Learned ASC for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question be quashed.
8. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.
Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No.77/2016, under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Sadar Bazar, Delhi, and the proceedings emanating therefrom
shall stand quashed.
9. The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
